brand: Hunt for masthead lockups pairing a small monospaced badge/chip (hairline border, elevated bg, 2–3px letter-spacing) with a large display-weight uppercase wordmark — the badge is a code-style abbrev anchoring identity, the wordmark carries the product name
Look for the three-tier horizontal composition at baseline alignment: [mono code chip] [display-font product name] [allcaps mono subtitle in secondary tone] — horizontal flow, NOT stacked rows
Prefer headers where the accent appears on exactly one element in the brand cluster (the chip fill or a single word/letter), leaving the rest in warm neutrals — accent scarcity is the quality signal

Sticky top-bar: brand cluster left, action buttons right, hairline bottom rule, bar tone slightly elevated from page ground — no heavy drop shadow, no full-bleed gradient, at most a faint 5% amber wash fading 80% down
step-heads: Hunt for numbered section dividers where the numeral is typographically isolated: mono or display-font, accent-colored, zero-padded (01/02/03), sitting at baseline with the section title — NOT boxed, NOT inside a circle, just inline flow

The structural triad: [accent numeral] + [display-font uppercase heading at line-height ≤1] + [subdued single-line descriptor at 13–14px in secondary tone] — total block height under 56px, tight vertical rhythm
Numeral must read as a semantic sequence marker not hero art — reject examples where numbers are oversized decorative elements with no hierarchical relationship to the heading
Prefer examples where the numeral and heading share a flex baseline-align row with a fixed 12–16px gap, so the number optically registers as a prefix rather than a separate element
terminal-preview: Hunt for terminal/shell output frames with a minimal titlebar containing: simplified traffic-light dots (flattened, muted, or only one active), a centered monospaced allcaps title, and an inline range slider with a value badge/readout showing the current setting

The two-tone structural split is the key pattern: titlebar at elevated panel tone + output area at a darker ground tone, both inside a single hairline-bordered outer frame with 2px radius — no rounded pill frame, no thick bezel

The column-width slider + readout badge pair is the distinguishing control — look for range inputs inline with a small token displaying the live value (e.g. '200 cols') in mono font with a hairline border
Accept frames with a faint footnote/disclaimer line at the bottom in mono secondary-tone type — this 'approximate rendering' footer is a live-preview configurator signature

acceptNuance: Typography carries hierarchy even without color: mono badges for code/IDs, Big-Shoulders-class display-weight uppercase for headings, regular-weight body — an example with no amber visible but correct typographic discipline should still score high

The 46px engineering crosshatch grid at hairline opacity is a signature substrate — accept any dark UI using grid, graph-paper, or dot-matrix background texture even if the grid color differs, because the pattern signals instrument-grade rather than consumer
Border-radius is a hard filter at 2px: reject any panel, card, or container with radius ≥8px — it immediately reads consumer app, not operator console, regardless of palette

Single-accent monovalence is a quality gate: if a UI uses more than one hue as a positive signal color it breaks Almanac Noir discipline — only amber-family accent plus one ember/alert hue reserved for destructive states is acceptable

The 5% amber-opacity header gradient fading to transparent over 80% is acceptable and desirable on the masthead — it is NOT the glassmorphism rejection criterion, which targets full-saturation multi-stop gradients and glow blooms
